clue.text: Innocent, not cold, but in a bad state to marry

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for cold is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: innocent means chaste, pure
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone pure but chilled is in a poor frame of mind to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'marry in haste, repent at leisure' makes hurry the bad state to marry in; 'but in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against wedding in a rush, so hurry is the condition in which marrying goes badly.

clue.text: Don't make use of second leg to score in this game

parts.words: Don't make use of second leg
parts.note: to hop is to move on one leg, not using the other
to scotch is to score or cut a line, as in an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: A rule of some playground game forbids using your other leg if you want to score.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTCH as a scored line is the old sense behind the game's name: the lines scratched on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a children's playground game of hopping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Excelled in description of Betelgeuse, say

definitions.meaning: an actor who excelled shone, played the lead role
Betelgeuse is a star, so it is literally star-like or star-marked

explanation.definitionFit: To star is to excel or take the lead; and something decorated with or being a star fits the bright giant in Orion.

clue.text: Time in opposition

definitions.meaning: the saying 'time is the ...' makes time a foe
opposition means the foe, the other side

explanation.definitionFit: A foe is the opposing side, and 'time is the foe' is a familiar saying.

clue.text: A comic ran wildly around in burlesque style

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of the words around it are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A comedian dashes about in a mocking, farcical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' shuffles A COMIC and RAN together; 'around' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaronic verse is comic burlesque writing mixing Latin with vernacular words.

clue.text: Dramatist killed in drunken row with meal

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A playwright met his end in a brawl over a meal fuelled by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' shuffles ROW with MEAL. The surface is true: the Elizabethan playwright was stabbed in a quarrel over a tavern bill in Deptford.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan playwright of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Able to get round a cutter

indicators.note: to get round says the word for able goes around the letter from the clue's a

parts.note: able means clever, skilled

explanation.surface: A capable person manages to dodge a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's chopper is a heavy cutting tool.

clue.text: Opportunity to resume progress, after falling in the heat

definitions.text: Opportunity to resume progress, after falling in the heat

parts.words: Opportunity to resume progress, after falling in the heat
parts.note: reads as a stumble in hot weather, but describes the extra race in rowing or cycling that gives losers of a heat a second chance to go through

explanation.definitionFit: In rowing and cycling it is an extra race letting heat losers qualify for the next round.

clue.text: Strangely inert, it is a salt

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next words are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, something unreactive turns out to be a salt.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a salt of nitrous acid, used in curing meat.

clue.text: Exult, gaining new honour

parts.note: to exult is to crow, boast in triumph

explanation.surface: Someone rejoices at receiving a fresh award.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal diadem symbolises supreme honour, and to award honour is to put a garland on a victor.

clue.text: Earth always round this feature of London streets?

parts.note: Earth is a planet

indicators.note: round says the word for always is turned about

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever, always

explanation.surface: The globe is forever circling some familiar sight on London's roads.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic contraction of 'ever'; 'round' turns it about. The question mark flags that the London plane is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is the hardy tree that lines a great many London roads.

clue.text: Pensioner seen lying around it, after retirement?

definitions.text: Pensioner seen lying around it, after retirement?

indicators.note: retirement suggests drawing back, so the combined letters are read backwards
lying around says the pensioner's letters are laid around the word it

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: A retired person is spotted lounging about outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying around' and 'after retirement' work in turn; the whole clue also pictures a pensioner idling on a paved terrace, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved terrace by a house is just where a retired person might lie in the sun.

clue.text: A criminal record will ring true

definitions.meaning: read literally, to have a past guilty verdict against you

explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means bearing a past guilty verdict; idiomatically it means being persuasive.

clue.text: A little morsel taken by perch?

definitions.text: A little morsel taken by perch?

parts.note: a tad means a little bit
a perch is an old measure of length, also called a pole or rod

explanation.surface: A small bite is snapped up by a freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: PERCH is both the fish and the old land measure equal to a pole; 'morsel taken by' links the wordplay and pictures a fish snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A young frog larva is a small titbit that a predatory fish like a perch would eat.

clue.text: In baffling way, it may give boy ulcers

indicators.note: may give says the letters can be rearranged to produce something new

explanation.surface: A mysterious remark that something might cause a lad stomach sores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it may give' says BOY ULCERS can be rearranged; 'it' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Done unclearly, so as to puzzle or confuse.

clue.text: Ruler bringing in a tester for poison, for example

indicators.note: bringing in says the ruler's letters take in the letter from the clue's a

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch introduces someone to taste food for toxins.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside REGENT. Not a royal food-taster: a chemist's substance used to detect, for instance, a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical used in testing to detect substances such as poisons.

clue.text: Tied house

parts.note: a tied house is a pub bound to one brewery, but read literally it is a knot named like a pub sign

explanation.definitionFit: It is an ornamental knot, tied; and it is a traditional pub name, a house.

clue.text: Demand to surrender and lay down arms? On the contrary

parts.words: and lay down arms? On the contrary
parts.note: laying down arms suggests limbs lowered, the opposite has them raised

explanation.surface: An order to give up the fight and drop weapons, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is not weapons but limbs: rather than put your hands down, raise them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the command shouted to make someone surrender, raising their arms.

clue.text: Colloquial expression one's unable to pronounce

definitions.text: Colloquial expression one's unable to pronounce

parts.words: Colloquial expression one's unable to pronounce
parts.note: reads as a phrase too hard to say, but means a slangy phrase you say when unable to help

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for 'I can't do that', said when refusing or unable.

clue.text: One casually fired ceramic's very fashionable

parts.note: ceramic pieces are pots, read with the 's
hot means very fashionable

explanation.surface: Fired pottery is very much in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' pretends to mean kiln-firing the pottery, but it is a gun fired carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A random shot taken without careful aim.

clue.text: Speaker's description of little bird

definitions.meaning: a small loudspeaker that reproduces high notes
a small bird that chirps could be called one that tweets

explanation.definitionFit: A high-frequency loudspeaker is named for chirping, and a small songbird chirps.

clue.text: In the Elements, originally, men mark something Euclid proved

indicators.note: In says the first letter of the word Elements goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: originally says take the first letter of Elements

explanation.surface: Euclid's Elements contain a proposition he demonstrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places the first letter of Elements inside the other pieces; 'originally' picks it. OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid's geometry is a chain of propositions, each proved from axioms.

clue.text: Touchy when play is dominated by bowler, say

indicators.note: dominated by here means the play is surrounded and held by the hat

parts.note: a bowler is a hat, and tile is slang for a hat
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A cricketer gets edgy when a bowler controls the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dominated by' places the play inside the hat. In cricket a bowler delivers the ball, which the surface trades on, but here it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy here means relating to the sense of feel.

clue.text: Remove men from board to recover from disaster

definitions.meaning: literally, lift chessmen or draughts off the board
idiomatically, rebuild life after a calamity

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, lifting game pieces off a board; idiomatically, restoring order after a crisis.

clue.text: One who's taken orders in the army

definitions.text: One who's taken orders in the army

parts.words: One who's taken orders in the army
parts.note: reads as any obedient soldier, but means someone ordained in holy orders serving as a forces chaplain

explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain is a priest, ordained in holy orders, who serves the forces.

clue.text: Sign of cold — but it could be nice on Madeira

definitions.meaning: ice forming is a sign of freezing weather

definitions.text: it could be nice on Madeira
definitions.meaning: Madeira cake is a British sponge cake, and a sugar topping would be nice on it

explanation.definitionFit: Ice forming on surfaces shows cold, and the sugar topping on cakes shares the word.

clue.text: Measure European Community originally introduced

indicators.note: introduced says that letter is put inside the word for the European

parts.note: a Dane is a European

indicators.note: originally says take the first letter of Community

explanation.surface: The European Community brought in a new regulation at first.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside DANE. 'Measure' is an old word for a stately dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old term for a dance, particularly a slow formal one.

clue.text: It could make birch die, sprayed round middle of field

definitions.text: It could make birch die, sprayed round middle of field

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the central letter
sprayed suggests scattering, so these letters are mixed up
middle of picks the central letter of the word field

explanation.surface: A weedkiller sprayed in a field could kill off a birch tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprayed' shuffles the tree and the verb, and 'round' wraps them about the centre of 'field'. The whole clue describes a weedkiller at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A weedkiller sprayed on plants can kill them, a birch included.

clue.text: Integrated community providing English with comfortable support

parts.note: cosy means comfortable
a stem supports a flower or leaf

explanation.surface: A close-knit group gives an Englishman a snug backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologically, it is a community of organisms interacting with their environment as one whole.

clue.text: Decided to reject a sinful weakness

indicators.note: to reject says the letter a is cast out of the word for decided

parts.note: decided means agreed, settled

explanation.surface: A committee resolves to turn down a sinful failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is one of the seven deadly sins, a moral failing.
